ai.description: *Chitra indica* reaches a carapace length of 1.1 meters. It features a flattened, olive-grey shell with intricate, wavy dark patterns and a narrow, elongated head with a tubular snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Chitra indica* is best distinguished by its narrow, elongated head with a distinct, tubular snout and a unique, intricate pattern of yellow vermiculations on its carapace.
ai.habitat: *Chitra indica* inhabits large, deep, slow-moving rivers with sandy or silty beds, typically found in low-altitude plains across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Indian narrow-headed softshell turtle is an active, opportunistic predator that primarily hunts by ambush, lying buried in riverbeds to snap at passing fish.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chitra indica* is oviparous, laying clutches of 65–187 spherical eggs in sandy riverbanks. Breeding occurs from late winter to spring (typically December to March).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Chitra indica* inhabits the major river systems of Northern and Central India, primarily across the Indo-Gangetic plains and the Indus basin at low elevations.
